c.pop: ~14,000 (permanent; swells seasonally with resort staff and visitors)
c.tagline: Canada's premier ski resort, a pedestrian village beneath twin Olympic peaks
langs: French (official Canadian second language, limited local use)

card: Widely accepted everywhere including tap-to-pay; cash rarely needed

taxi.fare: Metered; flat rates common for airport/Vancouver transfers
taxi.fareNote: Whistler Village itself is pedestrian-only, so taxis are mainly for outlying accommodations and Vancouver transfers

emergency.note: 911 reaches police, fire, and ambulance across Canada

english.label: Easy to get by in English

walk: Whistler Village is fully pedestrian and very walkable; Creekside and Function Junction require the free Whistler transit bus or a car

safety.safety: Very safe resort town with a strong tourism infrastructure
safety.crime: Minimal crime; main risks are mountain/backcountry related rather than urban
safety.note: Standard alpine safety precautions (avalanche awareness, sun/altitude exposure) apply for backcountry activities

hood_landmark.Whistler Village: Whistler Village Gondola base and pedestrian plazas
hood_landmark.Creekside: Creekside Gondola, the original 1966 base area
hood_landmark.Alta Lake / Lakeside: Alta Lake's beaches and canoe launches

avoid.reason: Theft of unattended skis, boards and bikes around the village is the main risk, and the Village Stroll gets rowdy after the bars close.

hood_desc: The bustling pedestrian heart of the resort with most shops, restaurants, and both main gondola bases; suits first-timers who want everything car-free.
A quieter cluster of ski-in/ski-out hotels directly beneath Blackcomb Mountain, a short walk or shuttle from the main village.
The original, more local base area a short drive south, with its own gondola, fewer crowds, and lower-key restaurants.
An industrial park turned craft-brewery and local-food hub south of the village, popular with residents and beer enthusiasts.
A residential lakeside area with beaches, canoe rentals, and mountain views, good for a quieter stay away from the village bustle.

water.note: Tap water is safe and comes from pristine mountain sources.

transit.sys: Whistler Transit System (free within-resort routes plus paid regional routes)
transit.pay: Free on village routes; cash or Compass-style fare on regional routes
transit.note: Whistler Village is pedestrian-only; the free shuttle covers Creekside, Upper Village, and Function Junction

transport.air: Vancouver International Airport (YVR), about 2 hr via the Sea to Sky Highway
transport.train: Rocky Mountaineer seasonal luxury rail service from Vancouver (not a commuter option)
transport.bus: Whistler Snowbus, Epic Rides, and YVR Skylynx shuttles run from Vancouver and the airport
transport.car: Scenic but occasionally snowy drive along Highway 99 (Sea to Sky Highway) from Vancouver

airport.name: Vancouver International Airport
airport.transport: YVR Skylynx shuttle, private transfer, or rental car

net.m: Strong 4G/5G in the village, patchier in the backcountry
net.w: Free wifi standard in hotels, cafes, and the village core
net.fwn: Free wifi widely available in the village
net.ap: A Canadian prepaid SIM or eSIM from Rogers/Bell/Telus

tip.s: 10-15% for ski instructors, guides, and spa staff
